items.stem: What does Amdahl's law tell us about parallel speedup?

options.text: The serial fraction of a program bounds the maximum achievable speedup regardless of core count
options.rationale: Correct: even small serial portions cap speedup.

options.text: Speedup grows linearly with cores without limit

options.rationale: Not once the serial fraction dominates.

options.text: Memory speed is irrelevant to speedup
options.rationale: Amdahl's law is about serial fraction, but memory still matters in practice.

items.explanation: Correct: even small serial portions cap speedup.

items.stem: Why does reordering nested loops to improve cache locality speed up a numerical kernel?

options.text: Accessing memory in a contiguous, cache-friendly order reduces costly cache misses
options.rationale: Correct: locality keeps data in fast cache levels.

options.text: It reduces the number of arithmetic operations
options.rationale: Loop reorder changes access order, not op count.

options.text: It eliminates the need for profiling
options.rationale: Profiling is still needed to target work.

items.explanation: Correct: locality keeps data in fast cache levels.

items.stem: Which statements about parallel computing are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Unsynchronised access to shared mutable data can cause a data race
options.rationale: Correct: races produce nondeterministic, incorrect results.

options.text: In distributed computing, excessive communication can dominate and limit scaling
Adding more cores always yields proportional, unlimited speedup
GPU offload has no data-transfer cost
options.rationale: False; host-device transfers are a real cost.
